title: Sliding Window Maximum
prompt:
Given `nums` and a window size `k`, return an array of the maximum in each window of `k` consecutive elements as the window slides left to right.

**Example**: `nums = [1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7]`, `k = 3` → `[3,3,5,5,6,7]`.

A **monotonic deque** of indices: keep it decreasing so the front is always the window's max, in O(n) total.
hints: Store INDICES in a deque, kept so their values are strictly decreasing front→back.
Before pushing i, pop from the back every index whose value is ≤ nums[i] (they can never be a max again).
Pop the front if it has slid out of the window (`front <= i - k`). Once `i >= k-1`, the front index holds this window's max.

solution.explanation: O(n): each index is pushed and popped at most once. Smaller values behind a bigger one are useless (the bigger one outlives them and dominates), so evicting them keeps the deque a decreasing sequence whose front is always the current window maximum.
